subject: general
question:
The kinetic energy of a moving object is dependent on which of the following quantities:

i) Mass of the body

ii) Square of the velocity

iii) Pressure
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Both (i) and (ii)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **kinetic energy** of a moving object is directly proportional to its **mass** and the **square of its velocity**.
 
• The formula for kinetic energy is given as **KE = (1/2) mv²**, where:
 
 
• **m** represents the mass of the object.
 
• **v** represents the velocity of the object.
 
 
 
• This implies that an increase in either the **mass** or the **velocity** (with velocity having a greater impact due to being squared) will result in an increase in the **kinetic energy**.
 
• **Pressure** does not have a direct relationship with kinetic energy in this context. Pressure is defined as **force per unit area** and pertains to different physical phenomena.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is that the kinetic energy depends on **both the mass of the body** and the **square of its velocity**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mass of the body**__

 __
 
• The **mass** is a scalar quantity that represents the amount of matter contained in an object.
 
• It is measured in **kilograms (kg)** in the SI unit system.
 
• In the context of kinetic energy, the mass determines the proportion of energy for a given velocity.
 
 
 
• **Square of the velocity**__
 __
 
• The **velocity** of an object refers to its speed in a specific direction and is a vector quantity.
 
• Since the velocity is squared in the formula, it has a larger influence on the kinetic energy than the mass.
 
• For example, doubling the velocity of an object will quadruple its kinetic energy.
 
 
 
• **Pressure**__
 
 
• **Pressure** is defined as the force exerted per unit area and is measured in **Pascals (Pa)**.
 
• It is unrelated to the kinetic energy of a moving object in this context.
 
• Pressure is often studied in the context of fluids, gases, and thermodynamics.
